answer: The vine multiplier is published, charged in timber, and nectar lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4615 identities would post 3374 proofs and burn roughly 53 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
